Celadon runs the projects, culture, and formation that carry Chinese-Filipino life on campus — and recruits the students who make them happen.

Established in 1985, Ateneo Celadon is the premier Chinese-Filipino organization of the Ateneo — developing members into globally and culturally sensitive members of society through festivals, leadership programs, and initiatives that deepen their understanding and appreciation of the Chinese-Filipino culture across 40+ years.

Established in 1985, Ateneo Celadon — often shortened to ADMU Celadon, ADMU CLDN, or Ateneo Cela — is the premier Chinese-Filipino organization of the Ateneo for 40 years running. We aspire to develop our members to become the game changers in society by integrating our vision of social change and deep cultural appreciation with the Chinese-Filipino tradition. In Celadon, we encourage our members to be united in this vision by developing their potential to become globally competitive and culturally sensitive leaders based on strong Chinese-Filipino principles.

We do this by showcasing our events such as cultural festivals, summits, and leadership programs that not only have won awards, but also bring out the best in our members — paving the way for them to become the leaders and visionaries of dialogue and community within a 'Greater Philippine Society'.

With the help of our partners such as the Ateneo Ricardo Leong Center for Chinese Studies, we believe this is possible. Simply put, Celadon has stayed and will stay true to its promise of being at the forefront of developing Chinese-Filipino identity, appreciation, and discourse.
Ateneo Celadon envisions a community that is deeply connected to Chinese-Filipino culture and is committed to engaging in its identity, appreciation, and discourse within greater Philippine society.

Ateneo Celadon strives to engage its members and audiences in learning, experiencing, and facilitating exchange between the Chinese-Filipino culture and greater Philippine society through culturally-rooted efforts. In line with this, the organization aims to develop member relations and equip them with different skills that are relevant to the practice and discourse of Chinese-Filipino culture.

Chinese-Filipino values are rooted in openness, sensitivity, excellence, and family.
This also includes the shared responsibility to understand, advocate for, and integrate Chinese-Filipino socio-cultural heritage.
